messages:
zoe: Quick check 5: we need a final decision for the long settings form validation. Options: inline-as-you-type, on-submit, or hybrid?

marc: Hybrid. Inline, lightweight hints on blur; show a concise top banner on submit with an issue count so users don't miss anything.

anya: Agree. For collapsed advanced blocks, show a small pill on the header (e.g., "1 issue"). On submit auto-expand the first errored block but don't steal focus.

carl: Accessibility: banner must be in an aria-live region. Use assertive on submit failure, polite for updates. Each field error should use aria-describedby and aria-invalid.

zoe: Copy: prefer "Fix 2 issues to continue." Actionable + shows scale. For typed-confirm cases: "Type DELETE to permanently remove 'Name'" in monospace.

marc: Destructive actions: policy suggestion - reversible items -> modal + undo (if infra supports soft-delete); irreversible customer data -> modal with typed-confirm. Document phases if undo backend isn't ready.

anya: UX nit: avoid auto-jumping when inline errors appear while tabbing. Mark errors inline but only move focus on explicit submit or when user clicks the banner.

carl: Dev constraints: debounce async checks (400-600ms) and surface "Checking..." state. If many errors (>4) collapse extra items under "Show all issues" to reduce overwhelm.

zoe: Tests to add: keyboard-only submit, screen reader announcement of banner and per-field messages, mobile sticky submit bar with error badge, collapsed-section pills, typed-confirm dialog SR behavior.

marc: I'll add three figma variants: immediate-inline, on-submit, hybrid. Tag @design for a quick review.

anya: Wrap-up: consensus on hybrid with phased rollout (banner + inline hints now, auto-expand & anchors next, typed-confirm + undo later). I'll write the RFC with acceptance criteria and handoffs.

aria-bot: Reminder: include automated checks for aria-live announcements and ensure color contrast for error text >= 4.5:1.
